To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conformation of the transmembrane domain 1 of mycobacterium phage holin, is dependent on the lipid concentration.

Pro-Gly-mediated conformational switch in the holin transmembranous domain is lipid concentration driven, and that this switch requires a central ProGly segment, and can be abolished upon mutation of Pro-Gly to Ala-Ala, or Pro-Ala.

(i) the transmembrane domain of the holin from the mycobacteriophages D29 and Bxz1 undergo a conformational switch between an α-helical and a β-sheet conformation, which is driven by lipid-to-peptide concentration, (ii) the conformational switch is mediated by a central Pro-Gyl residue, which acts as a molecular hinge, and (iii) this hinge is required for the reversibility of the conformational transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conformational behavior of a transmembrane peptide, the mycobacteriophase D29 holin.
the study of the conformational switch and its role in holin function.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of holin function, and how this relates to the conformational switch observed in synthetic TM domain I. The
